correctness.rationale: For any cubic prism a rich edge forces its own colour and its four adjacent colours to be pairwise distinct, establishing at least five. Explicit proper five-colour tables for n=3..9 were rechecked by standalone edge-incidence verification. All five-column local patterns suffice for rich-neighbor validity; the n=5,6,7 tables have identical four-column prefix, so every five-window crossing a concatenation seam equals a checked cyclic window of its preceding block. All n>=10 are sums of 5,6,7 with the explicit five-residue decomposition. Tests up to 500 and 1092 concatenations corroborate, but do not replace, this infinite proof. Computation path: verify.py.

originality.rationale: Published exact and general results were compared by implications and hypothesis checks, not titles. The 2026 three-times-edge-chromatic theorem and general seven-colour subcubic results are weaker; matching-of-three-vertices hypotheses fail for every cubic prism, and prior exact complete-(bi)partite formulae do not specialise. Semantic published-record and prior-claim comparisons found no identical prism result; inaccessible older full texts remain explicitly disclosed priority risks.
residual_risks: The original 2024 article and the 2025 five-colour subclass paper could not be inspected completely; neither accessible theorem implies this result, but undisclosed examples may exist.
A differently worded normal-edge-colouring or specialised prism construction might establish this equality without using rich-neighbor terminology.
No independent scientific audit or exhaustive historical-priority certification was performed.

value.rationale: A natural two-layer cycle family of connected cubic graphs has a sharp, uniform value five under a conjecture not yet proved for all connected subcubic graphs. This is not a bound for arbitrarily selected tiny examples: it covers infinitely many cubic graphs of unbounded order and provides a constructive linear-size block method, with a provably optimal lower bound. A five-column locality lemma makes the certified finite templates mathematically extensible.
